L530@P3: III. PREMISE OF THE LABELED MULTI-BERNOULLI
L531@P3: FILTER
L532@P3: In [10], an approximation to the Bayes multi-target filter
L533@P3: was proposed based on approximating the posterior as a
L534@P3: multi-Bernoulli RFS. Track labels were assigned to individual
L535@P3: components by post processing in order to estimate target
L536@P3: trajectories. Although the time prediction step was exact,
L537@P3: the data update approximated the posterior via the probability generating functional (PGFl) in two steps. The first
L538@P3: approximation expresses the posterior PGFl as a product of
L539@P3: legacy and updated terms which are not necessarily in multiBernoulli form (see eq. (18) in [10]). The second approximation chooses a multi-Bernoulli PGFl that matches the posterior
L540@P3: cardinality mean of the first PGFl approximation (see Section
L541@P3: III-C in [10]). This two stage approximation resulted in a
L542@P3: computationally inexpensive multi-target tracking filter which
L543@P3: was based on the assumption of a high signal-to-noise ratio
L544@P3: for sensor detections. Although performance was accurate in
L545@P3: such situations, a significant cardinality bias was observed
L546@P3: in harsher signal environments, due mainly to the first PGFl
L547@P3: approximation.
L548@P3: In [35], it was shown that the δ-GLMB density is closed
L549@P3: under the multi-target prediction and update operations. This
L550@P3: result was used to develop a δ-GLMB filter which formally
L551@P3: produces tracks. Moreover the only approximation used was
L552@P3: a direct truncation of the multi-target posterior rather than
L553@P3: approximating the multi-target PGFl. The only disadvantage
L554@P3: is that the tracking filter exhibits an exponential growth in
L555@P3: the number of posterior components. Tractable techniques for
L556@P3: truncating the posterior and prediction densities were proposed
L557@P3: based on the k-shortest paths [38], [39] and ranked assignment
L558@P3: algorithms [40]. The resultant δ-GLMB filter outperforms the
L559@P3: CPHD and multi-Bernoulli filters but is more computationally
L560@P3: expensive. See [35] for full details.
L561@P3: Using labeled multi-Bernoulli RFSs we can exploit the
L562@P3: intuitive mathematical structure of the multi-Bernoulli RFS,
L563@P3: without the weaknesses of the multi-Bernoulli filter, which
L564@P3: are that it does not formally produce track estimates and
L565@P3: exhibits cardinality bias. The premise of the proposed labeled
L566@P3: multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filter is the approximation of the
